messages:
Jess: Heads-up — proposing a small-but-impactful change to console telemetry: add a nullable `route_group_id` (string) to events for faster dashboard rollups and quota aggregation. Thinking dual-write + read-adapter for gradual rollout.
Sam: what's the main driver? dashboards or quota correctness?
Jess: both. Dashboards are slow because we JOIN route metadata on every query. If events carry route_group_id we can pre-aggregate cheaply and avoid expensive joins. Also quota windows need deterministic grouping.
Anya: I'm worried about increasing cardinality for storage and index bloat. Have we measured unique route groups per tenant?
Mike: quick numbers: on staging a tenant with many routes => ~8k distinct route_ids, route_group_id reduces to ~120 groups. It actually reduces downstream cardinality if we canonicalize groups.
Priya: dual-write concern: if we write both old and new envelopes we double ingest QPS briefly. Do we have burst capacity?
Jess: plan A: start with producer-side dual-write (event+envelopev2) flagged, write to AES-backed topic. Ingest will accept both and write events to events_v2 table with new column. Read-adapter will route queries to v2 for tenants opted-in.
Sam: fallback strategy if consumer fails?
Jess: fallback: consumers keep reading v1; we gate read-adapter behind a per-tenant feature flag. Also can switch producers back to v1 only if regressions.
Mike: can we avoid backfilling everything? Prefer to rely on read-adapter merging v1+v2 at query time for a while.
Jess: yes — read-adapter will UNION v1/v2 with v2 preferred. We can add a materialized view for heavy dashboards to converge later.
Priya: show me the DDL you'd run. index strategy?
Jess: SQL draft:
```sql
ALTER TABLE events_v2 ADD COLUMN route_group_id text;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ON events_v2(route_group_id) WHERE route_group_id IS NOT NULL;
-- avoid full-table lock, add column nullable then backfill in chunks
```
Anya: backfill plan? do we backfill synchronously or lazily on read?
Jess: lazy first: don't backfill historical rows. Producers populate new events going forward. For dashboards we can run targeted backfills per tenant for hot windows. Full backfill is optional and throttled.
Sam: how does this impact analytics jobs that full-scan events?
Mike: analytics ETL will read v2 topic or table. We need a migration to update downstream projections to prefer route_group_id when available.
Anya: quotas: if we switch grouping, need to preserve previous bucket semantics. Otherwise customers will see quota deltas.
Priya: we should create a compat layer: quota-service reads route_group_id if present, else falls back to route_id -> group_map. That means keeping route->group mapping up-to-date during rollout.
Jess: exactly. We'll ship a mapping service that keeps canonical group assignment and is updated by producers when group resolution happens.
ingest-bot: deploy-notice: producers-dualwrite flag will be available in canary tomorrow 09:00 UTC.
Sam: ops question — what about retention? Adding column increases row size; any impact on storage tiers?
Mike: negligible if we compress; but index footprint grows. We'll monitor p95 and storage per-tenant metrics. Add a rollout metric: new_column_write_rate and read_adapter_hit_rate.
Jess: UX for console: dashboards team — we can add an opt-in toggle per-organization to start using route_group rollups. That lets support validate before global flip.
Anya: timeline proposal?
Jess: Week 1: producer dual-write flag + schema deployed (nullable column + index concurrently). Week 2: enable dual-write for 10% tenants; read-adapter + metrics. Week 3: widen to 50%, run targeted backfills for top 10 tenants. Week 4: evaluate and decide global opt-in/backfill.
Priya: +1 but add a kill-switch and a safety playbook for backfill cancellation.
Mike: I'll add dashboards: per-tenant index bloat, query latency, adapter errors.
Jess: thanks — gonna drop this plan into the migration doc and open a PR. If anyone wants reviewer duty ping me.
Anya: ping me for the backfill playbook review.
Sam: will check quota-service compatibility and post a short checklist.
Jess: awesome — closing the loop here. :thumbsup:
